correctness.rationale: In the signed-permutation chamber x>=y>=z>=0 the extreme projections differ by 2(x+y), so the unit-edge width is (x+y)/sqrt(2). There are two positive vertex projections exactly when x>y+z, hence four edge crossings then and three otherwise. Around the width axis, area in latitude-height and azimuth coordinates is dw dphi. The chamber imposes w/sqrt(1-w^2)>=sqrt(3) cos(phi-delta); the section-type separator is phi=delta. The smaller-azimuth interval starts when the left side reaches 1, the larger-azimuth interval starts at sqrt(2), and the full azimuth range is allowed at sqrt(3). These give the stated thresholds and both interval lengths, with factor 48/(4pi). The level sets and projection-zero boundaries have area zero, so there are no omitted atoms. The upper-tail ratio is constant; in the intermediate interval the ratio has positive derivative in the decreasing angle theta. Independently, the opposite-sign probability for each edge is arccos(-1/3)/pi, confirming the two total masses. The calculation is exact and not based on a Monte Carlo fit.
residual_risks: Only unit-edge regular tetrahedra with central Haar orientations; no assertion for random affine sections. Conditional probabilities at isolated widths are versions of a density ratio.

value.rationale: The pairing of a support measurement with the combinatorial type of a cut is intrinsic to a single orientation of a canonical solid. The joint result gives a sharp forbidden interval for triangular sections and a non-null interval of exact independence (width-tail mass 6(1-sqrt(3)/2)), separated by a strictly varying type probability. Those facts are usable even when the two separate distributions are already known.
residual_risks: No generalization to arbitrary solids or statistical estimation claim is established.
